The Senior Pastor of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, Dr Paul Enenche, has reminded Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and Dino Melaye that they will account to God for how they use power and conduct themselves in the pursuit of political office. Enenche gave the warning on Friday during an all-night service at the church’s headquarters, the Glory Dome, in Abuja, where he invited the politicians and other representatives of political parties to pray for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a video of the session shared online, the cleric told the political figures that their actions in public office and their quest for power would eventually be subject to divine judgement. “I want all of us here and all that we represent to know that one day we will all stand before God. Everybody. To give the account of how we lived on it, what we did with power, around power, or in the quest for power. “All of us. That is the king of the universe. Bear that in mind. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “This life does not end here. Let’s talk to our political associates, talk to our political leaders, and talk to anyone we need to talk to. We will stand before God to account for our lives,” he said. He added that those who conducted themselves properly would have no reason to fear standing before God. The prayer session brought together Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress; Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement; and Melaye, a chieftain of the African Democratic Congress. Obi’s supporters should help fix his weaknesses – NDC campaign DG ‘May–July registrants to get PVCS in Dec’ INEC tests result transmission network for 2027 polls today They were joined by a representative of the All Progressives Congress and a member of the Peoples Democratic Party, reflecting the different political affiliations represented at the gathering. Enenche had earlier led the congregation in prayers for God’s will to prevail in Nigeria, credible elections, the proper functioning of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s electoral equipment and a peaceful election without bloodshed or post-election crisis. He also asked the politicians to greet one another despite their different party affiliations, urging them to demonstrate that political differences should not breed bitterness. The gathering was part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, founded in November 1996 by Enenche and his wife, Becky. The 2027 general elections are scheduled to begin with the presidential and National Assembly polls on January 16, while governorship and state assembly elections will hold on February 6. The Independent National Electoral Commission published a list of 18 presidential candidates, including President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress, Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement.
